findings.text: red-team lens, medium: If both competing runs post their notes within the same propagation window and each run's read-back executes before the other run's note is visible via the API, both runs see only their own note, both enter this branch, and both return `{"acquired": true}`, violating R1 ("exactly one proceeds"); none of the DSRACE requirements have a precondition covering this case, and the design's outside assumptions list ordering and stability of `created_at` but do not state that a comment is immediately visible to all API clients after the POST that created it. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "if [[ -z "$winner" || "$winner" == "$my_holder" ]]; then"; happens when: Two runs that add the label within milliseconds of each other on GitHub infrastructure where comment reads are served from a replica or cache that has not yet replicated the peer's newly posted note — a narrow but real condition on a busy GitHub host.; fix: design; ACCEPTED IF: the design's outside assumptions explicitly address cross-connection comment visibility consistency, or the design acknowledges the residual window where both runs proceed and states why it is acceptable)
